answer: Three established peers check the grain-warehouse license in the state agriculture registry, the surety bond, and a fresh signature before an agent can answer, because one license only lands after a facility inspection, a net-worth check, and a bonded warehouse full of real grain. Each fake pays $20,000 to $100,000 for its own bond and building, so a canyon of impostors costs $20 million before a single answer, like a jade vault that only stores one harvest at a time, and the nectar of a free answer is never free when every fake still pays for its own warehouse.
